record_notes.DCP-LETT-1581: August 25, 1854 is an incoming fragment, not a Royal Medal letter. Full surviving eight blocks cover Berkeley and hybrid peas, Lindley wheat, Hooker Meconopsis experiment, Jussieu and Brongniart reading, Binney fossil plants and high/low progression, Stonesfield mammals, Braun individuality with the seed argument, Leonard ears/Bowman, Erasmus health, request for the barnacle book and housing/job prospects. Darwin pencil additions are undated. The missing part plausibly contained further subjects answered in 1588, but its words are unavailable. Earlier June/July high-low letters are background, not a substitute for the missing immediate Darwin note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1588: September 7 with supplied 1854 year explicitly thanks Hooker long letter and answers several unique points in 1581: requested Barnacle Book and Rejuvenescence, seed individuality, and placental Stonesfield mammals. Some ten days ago describes the letter approximately, not an exact receipt date. P1 reports sending the books yesterday, not Hooker receipt. P2 explains Cryptophialus classification with uncertainty; P3–4 distinguish reading about individuality from having really read Braun. P5 thanks Huxley review, Nunn, Mrs Hooker Humboldt copy and discusses journal payment and Lancet treatment: much of this incoming material is missing. P6 is a prospective Liverpool trip; P7 promotes Westwood for a future medal; P8 plans renewed species work in a day or two. September 9 journal and 1855 award in apparatus are later events. No forwarding to Lyell and no aberrant-genera calculations occur in this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1629: Fragment begins mid-sentence about Murchison and Unger. November 3, 1854 is editorially inferred from the response; do not treat it as an original full dateline. Preserved subjects include Greenland correction and Lyall Arctic collection, Marianne Islands reference, prior aberrant-genera request not yet reworked, Ischia Cyperus/Pteris puzzle, Tuesday Linnean invitation, and recent Down/Crystal Palace visit. The request predates November 15 and may have been oral at Down; the quoted separate Darwin question and later list are distinct objects. Later Hooker publications and bibliography entries are not contemporary availability or guaranteed identification of every cited paper. Source 1597 answers P2, P5 and P6 despite catalogue-ID order.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1597: November 5 with supplied 1854 year. Medal congratulations P1–3 respond to news in an incoming note received yesterday, but that news is missing from surviving 1629. P4–6 explicitly answer the Greenland report, Ischia puzzle and Tuesday invitation in 1629; accept only that preserved response section. The incoming fragment date is inferred partly from this response, so the date is not independent proof of identity. November 4 receipt is explicit for the congratulatory note, but do not automatically assign it to all surviving 1629 material. Early insect-aberrance work is not proof of access to Waterhouse November 11 list.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1600: Incoming fragment dated editorially to Monday November 6, 1854, following Darwin November 5 refusal. Fossil leaves from Disco are described as apparently ordinary dicot leaves, not identified genera; future pine cones and planned botanical work remain prospective. Bentham returned and the aberrants are not forgotten. P4 announces taking a Richmond Hill house, distinct from December moving. P5 explains the Linnean invitation because Hooker thought Darwin would be in town; this answers 1597 P6. Darwin pencil prompts about Bentham, Barrande, Forbes and Comfort are separately attributed and undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1601: November 15 with supplied 1854 year explicitly thanks the Richmond Hill news in 1600. Only the first sentence of P1 is used as this direct prompt-response section; Bentham historical notes and Comfort employment have additional communications not preserved here. P2 witnesses Waterhouse aberrant-weevil list by its 62 genera and calculated means, without proving exact receipt or knowledge of every later annotation. P3–6 give Darwin independent Lindley calculations, exclusions and perplexing result, preserving his numbers as claims, not silently recomputed data. P7 doubts theory/fact agreement and proposes within-family comparisons; P8 wishes for a discussion of geography. The 1855 imprint on Bentham historical notes is not proof Darwin could not have received an advance copy in 1854. This outgoing letter does not establish same-day availability to Hooker for 1607.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1607: Wednesday is original; November 15, 1854 is inferred from a November 20 Darwin note, whose content is only described in the editorial footnote. Hooker says 80 anomalous genera but only 40 rows survive, as the footnote explicitly notes. The two counts are Steudel versus Hooker/Bentham estimates. P2 develops the distinct longitudinal Australia-split, climate, extinction and new-creation argument, with hypothetical assumptions retained. The request was already pending in 1629/1600, not uniquely identifiable with same-day 1601. Read all 40 rows and later Darwin notes: pinned November 30 note is dated; the additional calculation and pencil annotations are not assigned the incoming date. Raw HTML has literal totals 1161 1132 and MathML numerator 6722 / denominator 78005; the quoted footnote calculation claims 11.6. These are source rendering inconsistencies requiring later verification, not permission to invert fractions, remove leading digits or invent 40 missing rows. No inline figure exists.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1609: December 2 with supplied 1854 year. P1 distinguishes Darwin attendance at the medal presentation from second-hand praise of Hooker dinner speech; he did not hear that speech himself. P2 reports breakfast the next morning. P3 explicitly acknowledges both aberrant genera and Australian geography from 1607 but says he has not had time to consider them; that narrow acknowledgement is a direct response. Preserve the separate earlier dated notes in 1607 apparatus rather than flattening all consideration into one event. P5 sends to Hooker father because the Richmond address is unknown, not a new incoming address letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1610: December 4 with supplied 1854 year. P1–3 directly engage the Bentham list and distinctive Australia-splitting speculation in 1607, including concern that selecting only small genera biases the result. Darwin asks Hooker to query Bentham, discusses genus/family equivalence and withholds trust in the list. These are definite content matches, not merely adjacent letters. P4–5 asks for evidence/publication of Aquilegia unity from an earlier remark not preserved here. P6 reports reading Forbes tribute in Gardeners Chronicle; P7 hopes the move is comfortable, and P9 describes difficulty renting a London house. Later successful January tenancy is not December knowledge. Accept P1–3 as the response section; later independent topics remain separate grounding.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1611: December 5 with supplied 1854 year; incomplete incoming letter ends mid-sentence. Hooker answers the December 4 questions specifically, reports seeing Bentham today, distinguishes size alone from size plus natural-order status, warns about memorable large genera in a miscellaneous sample, argues rarity and anomaly may be circular, and suggests single-order comparisons. P4 quotes Darwin objection about splitting Australia and asks two alternative meanings. P5 sends unpublished Aquilegia results, explains imperfect proof and requests return; later publication and promised copy are not already received. The attached Darwin memorandum, later ink/pencil comments, and later Natural Selection quotations are not Hooker letter voice or automatically dated December 5. No Darwin receipt date is established by this reverse reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1573: Explicit accepted primary reading reused with matching note, ledger and source pins. June 27, 1854 answers 1572 across childbirth, Brodie, dinner and explicit highness/lowness question. Chloroform is a question to Hooker, not a reported Hooker action yet. Darwin states ideas are eclectic and unclear, distinguishes within-kingdom differentiation, cross-kingdom comparison, retrograde development and physiological division of labour; preserve qualifications rather than replace with a settled ranking. Footnote quotations from other works and modern histories are not the response body. Hooker 1576 answers the chloroform question and elaborates the taxonomy debate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1576: Explicit accepted primary reading reused with matching note, ledger and source pins. Thursday June 29, 1854 follows June 27 answer. Hooker says he administered chloroform despite doctor prejudice and explicitly opposes Darwin gales-of-wind analogy. He argues Coniferae are genuine dicotyledons, temporarily allows a gymnosperm/angiosperm division, asks for botanical sources and disputes parallel series using mollusc/articulate comparisons. His strict all-members hierarchical view is not Darwin agreement. Wife improving and Saturday Kew return prospective; horticultural prospectus seeks wealthy subscribers. Separate Darwin notes include genealogical comparison and distinction between degradation and non-development; undated notes are not Hooker words or June 29 Darwin response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1577: Explicit accepted primary reading reused with matching note, ledger and source pins. July 7, 1854 directly answers 1576: delay due to visitors and illness, joking elastic-theory objection, requested botanical references recalled uncertainly, disagreement about comparing archetypes, larval/degradation distinction, ancient forms resembling embryos, rejection of parallelism and Forbes polarity. Keep uncertain memory and wrong Jussieu volume in original; correction belongs to apparatus. P8 offers conditional subscription or advertisement forwarding, not completed subscription/delivery. Contemporary sickness and caveats remain. Later Origin formulation in footnote is not current available source material.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1598: Explicit accepted primary reading reused with matching note, ledger and source pins. November 11, 1854 incoming incomplete letter supplies aberrant weevil genera after a missing Darwin request and catalogue loan. Read the entire two-column list, continuation blocks and P10–20 discussion. Curly-bracket species counts, totals and corrections are Darwin later pencil annotations, not Waterhouse original list. Waterhouse admits a theoretical preference against tiny families despite his initial no-theory claim. He contrasts natural groups with single-character classification, discusses Brachycerus, Byrsops, Hipporhinus/Leptops and Australian Amycteridae, and cautions that sound distribution generalisations require sound classification. Unknown genera remain explicitly unknown. The separate-sheet warning not to read is historical prose, not an agent instruction. Diagram independently viewed; source label placement retained. Later Darwin notes and 1858 publication are not November 11 availability to Darwin.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Two antenna sketches: left nearly continuous curved segmented form labelled orthoceri; right sharply elbowed form labelled gonitoceri with a terminal club. The original printed leaders label club, scape and funiculus; preserve their placement as drawn, even where interpretation against the body definitions would be uncertain. Diagram shows contrasting arrangement, not a scale measurement or proof of taxonomic affinity.

Three current-period contexts and Waterhouse 1598 reuse explicit accepted root readings and visual observation with all pins checked.
